_comment: KIT TEMPLATE — install at .claude/settings.json. NOT drift-checked: every path,
matcher and twin below is this project's own. Read it and adapt it.
TIER 0 OF THE TOKEN ECONOMY. autoCompactWindow is the single highest-value line
in the whole setup and takes thirty seconds: without it every session pays the
default ~1M compaction window. It goes in at phase 0.2, BEFORE any source file
exists. See playbooks/3-TOKEN-ECONOMY.md §1.
statusLine is deliberately absent HERE and may not be for you: it is CLI-only and
is never invoked by the VS Code extension. An extension adopter who installs it
sees nothing and cannot tell unsupported from broken (2-SETUP-LAYOUT.md §2.1).
ONE HOOK, ONE QUESTION, so a failure in any of them is legible on its own.
bash-gate holds the irreversible shell acts and whatever constitutes deployment;
agent-write-scope bounds where a SUBAGENT may write, denies it a commit, and
decides who may spawn. Add a third only for a danger your census actually names —
a DDL gate written against a project with no database is a control that cannot
fire, and a gate that cannot fire reports green forever.
⚠ A HOOK FILE IS NOT A HOOK UNTIL THIS FILE WIRES IT. Every entry below must
match the @event and @matcher its hook file declares; check-hook-registration.mjs
reconciles all three and its selftest covers seven ways a hook can be unwired
while every artefact still says it exists.
⚠ HOOKS ARE READ AT SESSION START. A hook installed mid-session does nothing for
that session — it will pass its own probes from the command line while the
session that wrote it keeps prompting on every command. Restart (L-64).
TWINS are the settings-layer fallback for when a hook is dead, and each is named in
the fallback of the bash-gate rule it backs (its fallbacks region). They are NOT
dormant while the hook lives: the permissions docs (read 2026-09-11) say an ask rule
still prompts under a hook allow and a deny still blocks — life-therapy measured
otherwise on 2026-08-18. So do NOT add a twin that is wrong in the opposite direction
to its rule: Bash(git push --force*) also matches --force-with-lease, which the hook
allows; Bash(git push --force *), with the space, does not. Write a trailing :* or
a spaced *: Bash(git merge:*main*) has a literal colon and matches NO command, and
the two twins below read that way until 2026-09-11. agent-write-scope has NO twin and CANNOT have
one: a permissions rule has no agent dimension, so it cannot say 'only when the
caller is a subagent'. Its probe suite is the backstop instead.
CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH pins Main → parent → child. The platform
default is 3, which lets a spawned child fan out again. THE CAP MUST LAND IN THE
SAME CHANGE AS THE Agent GRANT it constrains — the first adoption propagated the
census spine (which carries the grant) and not the cap, and ran a day with an
unbounded fan-out available. That split is exactly what 4-AGENT-PIPELINES.md
warns against, and it is L-63: the propagation unit is the contract, not the
files that changed.
⚠ DENY PowerShell, and keep it denied (M-KIT-22). On Windows the harness offers a
PowerShell tool BESIDE Bash — on some machines as the primary shell — and every hook
matcher above says `Bash`. A command-gate that one tool bypasses is not a gate: the
lethal set, the install ban and the branch twins all go quiet for the tool the agent
may prefer. Do not widen the matcher instead — bash-gate parses POSIX tokens, and a
POSIX parser over PowerShell syntax is partial coverage that reads as whole. The Bash
tool exists on every platform, so one shell, gated. check-kit-drift asserts this line.
